alternatives.reason_rejected: Works (verified via headless probe when written to disabledMcpServers in ~/.claude.json) but is per-user per-machine — does not satisfy the apply-to-all-users requirement; kept as the documented fallback for testers
Empirically does nothing for plugin-bundled servers — user restarted and both servers still ran; the mcpjson in the key name is literal

assumptions: deniedMcpServers merging from project settings is verified on Claude Code 2.1.205; it is documented primarily as an enterprise key and could narrow in a future CLI release
the deny's command array must exactly match the plugin's pin — a future plugin pin bump silently un-denies until the array is updated
context: Superseded the disabledMcpjsonServers fix — it silently does nothing for plugin servers. Replaced with checked-in deniedMcpServers serverCommand deny in .claude/settings.json; verified plugin server no longer loads
rationale: Root cause of the failed first fix: disabledMcpjsonServers only governs project .mcp.json servers — the CLI's own embedded help text says plugin/user-scope servers are disabled via /mcp disable, persisting to disabledMcpServers in the ~/.claude.json project entry (per-user, not committable). The committable mechanism is deniedMcpServers, whose deny check reads merged settings from all sources (verified in CLI 2.1.205 binary: only the allowlist is managed-only). Matched by serverCommand rather than serverName because both servers are literally named 'twining' — a name deny could hit the @next server too; the exact 1.x launch command targets only the plugin's copy. Verified: with the per-user disable removed and only the checked-in deny active, claude mcp list shows only the @next server.
summary: Chose checked-in deniedMcpServers serverCommand deny over per-user /mcp disable or the ineffective disabledMcpjsonServers key
